findings.title: Org slug condition inverted by the "cleanup" rewrite
findings.body: The original was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`. The new line is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which drops the `!`. Now the slug is written immediately only when team billing is enabled. In that case `requestedSlug` is also stored for the later verified flow. With billing disabled, the organization is created with no slug at all. This change has nothing to do with multiple destination calendars. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, or drop the hunk from this PR.

findings.title: TypeError for Google Meet location when there is no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty. `handleNewBooking` can set it to `null` (lines 1063-1067), and the other call sites now pass `[]`. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without `?.`, so it throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. It only runs when `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. That is exactly the case the fallback to Cal Video is meant for, a Meet location with no Google calendar. The original code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references lose their credentialId
findings.body: Before, `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. Now `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. For non-calendar results (video/Cal Video/Zoom/Meet), `result.credentialId` is set by `videoClient.createMeeting` (packages/core/videoClient.ts:78). The reference is now persisted with no credentialId, so anything that resolves the video credential from the reference loses it. The calendar branch is the only one that needed to change, so keep `: result.credentialId` in the else branch.

findings.title: updateLocation now stores references with no externalCalendarId/credentialId
findings.body: `updateLocation` builds `referencesToCreate` from `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. `CalendarManager.updateEvent` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-322) does not return `externalId` or `credentialId`, so for calendar results both are `undefined`. Before, they came from `evt.destinationCalendar`. `editLocation.handler.ts:113-122` writes these as new `references.create` rows without deleting the old ones. After a location edit the booking therefore gets calendar references without a calendar ID or credential. Later updates and cancels then fall into the legacy 'try every credential' path, and Google falls back to `primary`. Have `updateEvent` return `externalId` and `credentialId`, or reuse the existing reference values.

findings.title: Destination calendars without credentialId create the event but record no externalCalendarId
findings.body: In the `else` branch (destination without `credentialId`, lines 375-381) `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `externalId`. `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `externalId: undefined` and `create()` stores `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`. The reference is saved without the calendar ID that `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` used to provide. The same applies to the 'first connected calendar' fallback and the `other_calendar` branch. Pass `destination.externalId` in the legacy branch too.

findings.title: Error in updateAllCalendarEvents is no longer logged
findings.body: The `console.error(message)` call was removed from the catch block, so `message` is built and never used. Any exception while updating calendar events (for example the new `prisma.credential.findUnique` fallback, or `updateEvent` with an undefined credential) is swallowed and returned as `success:false, appName:'none'` with nothing in the logs. Restore the `console.error` or use `log.error`.

findings.title: Fallback lookup compares externalId to itself and can never match
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. In the else branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `find` looks for a calendar whose `externalId` equals that falsy value and always returns `undefined`. The same pattern is at lines 315-317 in `deleteEvent`. The old fallback to `destinationCalendar.externalId` is gone. For legacy bookings with no `externalCalendarId` on the reference, update goes to an undefined calendar, and delete goes to `primary` instead of the booking's destination calendar. Use the first destination calendar (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`) as the fallback.

findings.title: createEvent ignores destination calendars that have no matching credentialId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` is now the `externalId` of the destination whose `credentialId === credentialId`, otherwise `primary`. A destination calendar with `credentialId` null (the legacy branch in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, lines 375-381, keys on `integration`) never matches. The event is created on the user's primary calendar rather than the selected one, where before `destinationCalendar.externalId` was used. Also, the `externalId` that `EventManager` passes to `CalendarManager.createEvent` is never given to the service. Fall back to the destination matching by `integration`, or to the first destination calendar.

findings.title: Collective team members' destination calendars are silently dropped when the organizer/event type has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (lines 1063-1067). `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is then a no-op, so the other collective hosts' calendars are never used. Build the array first (`[...(base ? [base] : []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) instead of mutating a possibly-null value. Also note that `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled as a side effect inside an async `map` callback; it works only because the push happens before the first `await`.

findings.title: Unrelated rewrite of loadUsers changes behavior
findings.body: The `loadUsers` rewrite is unrelated to destination calendars. It drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user select, although `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 355) still requires `organization: { slug }`. It throws on an empty `dynamicUserList`. It also rewraps every error as a 400/500 `HttpError`, hiding original status codes, and returns `eventType.users` without the old `|| []`. The `isTeamEventType` and `orginalBookingDuration` changes are the same kind of drive-by edit. Split these out, or at least keep the `organization` select.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel block now runs once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch (lines 444-468) deletes the first calendar reference of every remaining booking, across every calendar credential of the user. It now sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. With N calendar references on a booking, all remaining events are deleted N times, producing N-1 redundant API calls and 404/410 errors from the provider. Run it once, outside the per-reference loop.

contracts.action: EventManager.create builds booking references from CalendarManager.createEvent results (externalId/credentialId)
contracts.equivalent_path: Old code read evt.destinationCalendar.externalId/credentialId; CalendarManager.createEvent now echoes the externalId argument and credential.id.
contracts.before_after: Before: one destination calendar determined the reference fields for all results. After: each result carries its own externalId/credentialId, but only the credentialId-bearing destination branch passes externalId, and the non-calendar branch drops credentialId.
contracts.visible_effect: Booking references persisted on the booking decide which calendar and credential are touched on later update and cancel.
contracts.failure_mode: Legacy/no-credentialId branches and video results store references with missing externalCalendarId or credentialId, with no error or log.

contracts.action: EventManager.updateLocation writes references from calendar update results
contracts.equivalent_path: editLocation.handler persists updatedResult.referencesToCreate via booking.update references.create
contracts.before_after: Before: externalCalendarId/credentialId came from evt.destinationCalendar. After: from result.externalId/credentialId, which CalendarManager.updateEvent never sets.
contracts.visible_effect: After an edit-location, the booking gains calendar references with null externalCalendarId and credentialId.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent loss of the calendar and credential link on the booking.

contracts.action: New prisma.credential.findUnique fallback in createAllCalendarEvents / updateAllCalendarEvents / handleCancelBooking
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously only this.calendarCredentials (the organizer's) or bookingToDelete.user.credentials were searched.
contracts.before_after: Credentials for other team members are now loaded by id from the DB, and the credential row with its key is passed to getCalendar.
contracts.visible_effect: Team-member calendars can get events created, updated and deleted.
contracts.failure_mode: If the credential is not found, create skips it silently; update passes an undefined credential and throws in CalendarManager.updateEvent (credential.appName), and the catch no longer logs.

summary:
The multi-destination-calendar refactor has two blockers. `EventManager.ts:119` throws a TypeError for a Google Meet location with no destination calendar. `create.handler.ts` inverts the org slug condition (the `!` was dropped). I also found several regressions that fail silently:
- Video references lose their credentialId.
- `updateLocation` stores calendar references with no externalCalendarId or credentialId.
- Google `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` fall back through a lookup that can never match.
- Google `createEvent` ignores destination calendars with no credentialId.
- Collective team members' calendars are dropped when there is no base destination calendar.
- `updateAllCalendarEvents` no longer logs errors.

The `loadUsers` rewrite in `handleNewBooking.ts` is unrelated scope, and the recurring-cancel block now runs once per calendar reference. I read the files by hand and did not run tests or the code.
